name: Shebuel
overview: Shebuel was a male Levite who served in the worship ministry during the time of the temple musicians. As the son of Heman, he was set apart to prophesy with musical instruments such as lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was notably chosen as the thirteenth by lot among the singers, highlighting his specific role within the organized group of temple musicians.
namesAndTitles: The name Shebuel likely means 'captive of God' or 'God restores,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's intervention or deliverance. This proper name, as recorded, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotations.
familyAndRelationships: Shebuel is explicitly identified as the son of Heman, situating him within a prominent Levitical family known for temple service. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any additional family connections for Shebuel.
scriptureSignificance: Shebuel's importance lies in his role within the Levitical musicians who were dedicated to prophesying through music and worship. Being chosen by lot as the thirteenth singer underscores the ordered and divinely guided nature of temple worship. His service alongside instruments like lyres, harps, and cymbals reflects the biblical emphasis on music as a means of prophetic expression and praise to God.
